newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady, INRO not a factor.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady, INRO not a factor.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed steady on Friday with news that the International Natural Rubber Organization (INRO) is now set to resume intervening in the market largely ignored by the trade, dealers said.
"Nobody talked about INRO in this market. Trading this day was very light and dull. All the major consumers were sidelined," a dealer said.

"There was some buying for RSS3 by some Europeans doing their routine covering. There was also several hundred tonnes of TSR20 hit in the ring session. The INRO report had no impact at all," another trader said.

Another dealer said there should be no impact in the trade to the INRO news because prices have not yet approached a level where it would have to intervene even though they have slid to a 36-month low last April.
"It's just a statement of what the market already knows," a dealer said.

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was seen unchanged at 112.50 U.S. cents a kg. July RSS1 was indicated at 159.50 Singapore cents (US$1.12) a kg from 160.00 cents. July TSR20 was seen at 149.50 Singapore cents (US$1.05) a kg from 148.50 cents.
